groups.title: Rating
groups.intro: Star ratings on profiles.

flags.text: .fm-rating is a custom class, listed in Foundations › Filmmakers classes.

rules.text: A rating from 1 to 5. Editable on a profile, read-only in lists and summaries. Used on Sedcard (Summary view).
The stars sit in a role="radiogroup" with aria-labelledby pointing at a visible label that says what is rated (for example “Text fluency”). Each star’s radio has aria-label="n out of 5 stars".
The rating applies as it changes; no confirm step.

Keyboard: Tab moves into the group and out to the next field. Right and Up add one star, Left and Down remove one (down to 0), Home sets 0 and End sets 5. Bootstrap’s focus ring shows on the focused star.
The current value shows as text after the stars (“4 stars”, “1 star”, “0 stars” when cleared). No tooltips on the stars.

The value text is in an aria-live="polite" region, so screen readers announce each change. The radios keep their full names (“4 out of 5 stars”), so the scale is still announced. Tooltips are not needed: each radio already has its name, and tooltips only appear on mouse hover.
Fill shows the state: every star up to the chosen one is filled, the rest are outline, and hovering previews a rating.
Never colour alone. Stars are the body text colour, which passes 15:1 on white and grey.
Filled stars are fa-solid, the rest fa-regular. filmmakers.css does the fill and hover preview with CSS only (.fm-rating) and sets the star colour to --bs-fg-body on .fm-rating.

Stars use btn-xs with no gap between stars, which keeps the control compact for desktop, where most people use it. Do not go smaller. The star icons are the body text size (14px), as in production, in both the editable and the read-only rating.
btn-xs gives each star a 24px target, the WCAG 2.2 AA minimum (2.5.8, 24 by 24px).
When a rating is set, a Tertiary Clear rating button follows the value; it hides when there is no rating.
In a form: help text and errors are linked with aria-describedby, an error sets aria-invalid="true", and a required rating sets aria-required="true" on the radiogroup (see Validation).
Read-only: the label, then lighter stars, so a read-only rating does not look clickable. Two sizes: 14px by default, and 12px (label included) in dense lists and tables. Keep it on one line.
Read-only stars pass 5.2:1 or more on white and grey. They carry a title and a visually hidden “n out of 5 stars”.
Left aligned in its row, so nothing moves when the value text or Clear rating changes.

rules.text: A short task or decision on top of the page: one decision, or a form of about six fields. Bootstrap 6 Dialog, built on the native dialog element, which traps focus, closes on Esc and returns focus to the button that opened it.
Label it with aria-labelledby pointing at the title.
Only for one short decision or a form of about six fields. Anything multi-step or needing its own URL is a page. Dialogs never open dialogs, never stack and never appear unprompted.
Dialogs may scroll. When the content can be longer than the window, the body scrolls and the header and footer stay fixed, so the actions are always visible.
Add .dialog-scrollable (Bootstrap’s default) for a scrolling body, and give the scrolling body tabindex="0" so keyboard users can scroll it.
Sizes: the default (500px) for most; .dialog-lg (800px) for a six-field form. No extra large or fullscreen dialogs: use a page.
Footer: Cancel (Secondary) then the action, which names the outcome (“Save name”, never “OK” or “Submit”).
The close button has aria-label="Close".
Focus: the first field gets focus when a form opens (autofocus); a confirmation focuses Cancel. Focus is trapped inside while open and returns to the button that opened the dialog when it closes.
Forms: a click outside does not close the dialog, so nothing typed is lost. A dialog with an invalid field stays open and keeps the input (see Validation).

Confirming an irreversible action (Destructive actions): the title is a question naming the action and object (“Delete invoice INV-4021?”); the body says what is lost and that it cannot be undone; the danger action repeats the verb (“Delete invoice”) with an icon. Cancel and the action sit at opposite ends of the footer.
In a confirmation, the danger action has an icon so danger is not colour alone. Cancel has focus when the dialog opens (autofocus). Esc cancels, never confirms.
Reversible actions never get a confirmation dialog: act at once and offer Undo in a Toast.
Form dialogs use data-bs-backdrop="static".

rules.text: A list of production entities, such as Auditions and Selections. Each row has a title, one to four columns that the page supplies, and an Action gutter. One shell for every such list.
Every row in a list shares one grid-template-columns, so the columns line up.
The list has role="list" and each row role="listitem".
The title is the row’s link, weight 600, followed by a .fg-3 meta suffix at the same size: (open), (Rank: #2). The whole row is not clickable. No italics for state.
Media: a fixed 132px, 16:9 thumbnail in every list that has media (as in production). When an item has no image, show the placeholder with a monitor icon. Lists without media leave the column out.
The thumbnail’s alt is the title.
Details sit on one line that wraps: the type as icon + weight 600 label in sentence case (not all-caps), the visibility as icon + text, then the stats.
Stats are icon + value. Icons inherit the text colour; success only for a state such as Selection status. Primary never tints icons or headings.
Each has a visually hidden label and a tooltip with the same name (e.g. Roles, Invitations), and is focusable so the tooltip opens on keyboard focus too.
Short labels such as R: and A: are .fg-3, with the full words (Recording period, Airing) as visually hidden text.
Client visibility is an eye in the client zone colour when clients can see the content, and a .fg-3 eye-slash when they cannot, each with a tooltip and hidden text that say so.

The last column is the Action gutter (140–180px, one width per list), filling the row height, with Row actions stacked: Edit first, at most three visible, More last. Archive and Delete, or Remove, go in More with their explanation as a visible description. Delete is last, after a divider; a Remove that isn’t possible yet is disabled, with the reason.

When the card is under 900px wide, the row reflows: cells wrap onto new lines and the Action gutter becomes a bar along the bottom with the actions in a row at the end, like the Project card. No sideways scrolling.
